## Update

Inside thixos:
```shell
sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake ~/src/github.com/tteggel/.dotfiles#thixos
```
(Inside yoloixos this is intentionally impossible.)

## WSL networking and authentication

`config/wslconfig` selects Consomme. Mirrored mode previously dropped the guest's
default route on Wi-Fi NIC events, so switching back can reintroduce that problem.

Firebase's browser login normally opens a dual-stack `[::]` callback listener.
Consomme currently refuses IPv4 connections to that listener and hangs forwarding
IPv6 from Windows ([WSL#41860](https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/issues/41860)).
`home/home.nix` patches Firebase to listen on `127.0.0.1` instead; both
`firebase login --reauth` and `gcloud-reauth` use that package. The substitution
fails the build if upstream changes the listener, so the workaround gets reviewed
on upgrades. Before rebuilding, `firebase login --reauth --no-localhost` bypasses
the callback entirely using Firebase's supported code-paste flow.

For a complete outage, collect evidence **before** restarting anything. Home
Manager installs a Windows-side tool that remains available when WSL is broken.
Run from Windows PowerShell after rebuilding:

```powershell
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\wsl-network\wsl-network.ps1"
```

Reports go to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\wsl-network\reports`. They compare Windows and
guest HTTPS requests by hostname and IP, and record routes, DNS ownership,
firewall policy, host services and recent Windows networking errors. Individual
WSL commands time out so a stuck guest does not block the rest of the report.
Use `-Distro <name>` if the distro was imported under another name.

If only hostname requests fail, inspect DNS: WSL and Tailscale have both been
observed rewriting `/etc/resolv.conf`. If guest requests to IPs fail while the
Windows probes work, the WSL backend or filtering path is implicated. If both
fail, investigate the Windows connection; Windows logged Wi-Fi limited-connectivity
recovery and DNS timeouts during the October 2026 investigation. A healthy
snapshot had outbound/loopback allowed and no explicit Windows block rules;
this does not establish what happened during an earlier outage.

To try recovery without rebooting Windows, save work in **all** WSL distros,
then run from **elevated Windows PowerShell**:

```powershell
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\wsl-network\wsl-network.ps1" -Recover
```

This captures a report, runs `wsl --shutdown`, then restarts the Windows
`WslService` (or legacy `LxssManager`). Terminating/rebooting one guest leaves
host services running. Reopen WSL and run the report again to check recovery.
The service restart is a recovery attempt; the intermittent outage's cause
has not yet been reproduced. Firewall policy is unchanged.

## Embedded debug probes (USB/IP passthrough)

`thixos` forwards a USB debug probe from Windows into WSL over USB/IP, so you can
flash/debug ARM/RISC-V targets (e.g. a Pico running `debugprobe` firmware wired to
a target Pico 2 / RP2350 over SWD). `nixos/embedded.nix` provides **only the USB
plumbing**: the `wsl.usbip` client, the `vhci_hcd` kernel module, an auto-attach
service, and a udev rule giving `thom` (via `plugdev`) non-root access to the probe.
**The toolchain (probe-rs etc.) lives in your project's devshell, not the system.**

### One-time setup

On Windows (admin PowerShell) — install the USB/IP daemon and share the probe:
```powershell
winget install usbipd
usbipd list                  # note the BUSID of your probe, e.g. 3-1
usbipd bind --busid <BUSID>  # plain bind — NOT --force (see Troubleshooting)
```
Set `autoAttach = [ "<BUSID>" ];` in `nixos/embedded.nix`, rebuild, then restart
WSL once (the restart loads `vhci_hcd` and applies the `plugdev` group):
```shell
sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake ~/src/github.com/tteggel/.dotfiles#thixos

# Run from Windows PowerShell. The default only collects diagnostics.
# -Recover also shuts down ALL WSL distros and restarts the host WSL service.
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [ValidatePattern('^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$')]
    [string]$Distro = 'thixos',
    [switch]$Recover,
    [string]$OutputDirectory = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\wsl-network\reports"
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

if ($Recover) {
    $identity = [Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()
    $principal = New-Object Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal($identity)
    if (-not $principal.IsInRole([Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole]::Administrator)) {
        throw '-Recover requires an elevated Windows PowerShell window.'
    }
}

# A stuck WSL client must not prevent host diagnostics or service recovery.
function Invoke-BoundedCommand {
    param([string]$FilePath, [string]$Arguments, [int]$TimeoutSeconds = 20)
    $stdout = [IO.Path]::GetTempFileName()
    $stderr = [IO.Path]::GetTempFileName()
    try {
        $process = Start-Process -FilePath $FilePath -ArgumentList $Arguments `
            -NoNewWindow -PassThru -RedirectStandardOutput $stdout -RedirectStandardError $stderr
        # Cache the native handle before waiting so Windows PowerShell 5.1
        # retains the exit code even for very short-lived commands.
        $null = $process.Handle
        if (-not $process.WaitForExit($TimeoutSeconds * 1000)) {
            Stop-Process -Id $process.Id -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            Write-Output "Timed out after ${TimeoutSeconds}s: $FilePath $Arguments"
        } else {
            Write-Output "Exit code: $($process.ExitCode)"
        }
        # wsl --version emits UTF-16 on some versions, including without a BOM.
        Get-Content $stdout, $stderr -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object { $_ -replace "`0", '' }
    } finally {
        Remove-Item $stdout, $stderr -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    }
}

function Write-Section {
    param([string]$Name, [scriptblock]$Action)
    Write-Output "`n=== $Name ==="
    try { & $Action | Out-String -Width 200 | Write-Output }
    catch { Write-Output $_.Exception.Message }
}

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $OutputDirectory -Force | Out-Null
$report = Join-Path $OutputDirectory ("wsl-network-{0}.txt" -f (Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd-HHmmss-fff'))
Start-Transcript -Path $report | Out-Null
try {
    Write-Section 'Time and WSL version' {
        Get-Date -Format o
        Invoke-BoundedCommand wsl.exe '--version'
        Invoke-BoundedCommand wsl.exe '--list --verbose'
        Get-Content "$env:USERPROFILE\.wslconfig"
    }
    Write-Section 'Host services and WSL processes' {
        Get-Service WslService, LxssManager, hns, vmcompute, MpsSvc, WinNat -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
            Format-Table Name, Status, StartType
        Get-Process wslservice, wslhost, wslrelay, dllhost, vmcompute -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
            Format-Table Name, Id, StartTime, Handles
    }
    Write-Section 'Host adapters, routes and DNS' {
        Get-NetAdapter | Format-Table Name, InterfaceDescription, Status, LinkSpeed
        Get-NetRoute -DestinationPrefix '0.0.0.0/0', '::/0' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
            Format-Table InterfaceAlias, DestinationPrefix, NextHop, RouteMetric
        Get-DnsClientServerAddress | Format-Table InterfaceAlias, AddressFamily, ServerAddresses
    }
    Write-Section 'Host HTTPS by name' {
        Invoke-BoundedCommand curl.exe '--noproxy "*" --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 8 --head --silent --show-error https://example.com'
    }
    Write-Section 'Host TCP/TLS without DNS' {
        Invoke-BoundedCommand curl.exe '--noproxy "*" --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 8 --head --silent --show-error https://1.1.1.1'
    }
    Write-Section 'Guest addresses, routes and DNS ownership' {
        Invoke-BoundedCommand wsl.exe "--distribution $Distro --exec sh -c `"ip -brief address; ip route; ip -6 route; ls -l /etc/resolv.conf; cat /etc/resolv.conf; tailscale status`""
    }
    Write-Section 'Guest HTTPS by name' {
        Invoke-BoundedCommand wsl.exe "--distribution $Distro --exec sh -lc `"curl --noproxy '*' --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 8 --head --silent --show-error https://example.com`""
    }
    Write-Section 'Guest TCP/TLS without DNS' {
        Invoke-BoundedCommand wsl.exe "--distribution $Distro --exec sh -lc `"curl --noproxy '*' --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 8 --head --silent --show-error https://1.1.1.1`""
    }
    Write-Section 'Active host firewall profiles and explicit block rules' {
        Get-NetFirewallProfile -PolicyStore ActiveStore |
            Format-Table Name, Enabled, DefaultInboundAction, DefaultOutboundAction, AllowLocalFirewallRules
        Get-NetFirewallRule -PolicyStore ActiveStore -Enabled True -Action Block -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
            Format-Table DisplayName, Direction, Profile, PolicyStoreSourceType
    }
    Write-Section 'Active WSL Hyper-V firewall policy' {
        $wslId = '{40E0AC32-46A5-438A-A0B2-2B479E8F2E90}'
        Get-NetFirewallHyperVVMSetting -PolicyStore ActiveStore -Name $wslId |
            Format-List Name, Enabled, DefaultInboundAction, DefaultOutboundAction, LoopbackEnabled, AllowHostPolicyMerge
        Get-NetFirewallHyperVRule -PolicyStore ActiveStore -VMCreatorId $wslId -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
            Format-Table Name, Direction, Action, Protocol, LocalPorts, RemotePorts
    }
    Write-Section 'Recent host network and service warnings/errors' {
        Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='System'; StartTime=(Get-Date).AddHours(-24); Level=1,2,3} -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
            Where-Object { $_.ProviderName -match 'Tcpip|DNS|HNS|Host-Network|Hyper-V|Netwtw|NDIS|WLAN|Service Control' } |
            Select-Object -First 50 TimeCreated, ProviderName, Id, Message | Format-List
    }
    if ($Recover) {
        Write-Output 'Stopping all WSL distros, then restarting the Windows WSL service.'
        Invoke-BoundedCommand wsl.exe '--shutdown'
        $service = Get-Service WslService -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        if (-not $service) { $service = Get-Service LxssManager }
        Restart-Service -InputObject $service -Force
        $service.WaitForStatus('Running', [TimeSpan]::FromSeconds(30))
        Write-Output 'WSL service restarted. Reopen the distro, then run this report again to verify connectivity.'
    }
} finally {
    Stop-Transcript | Out-Null
}

content.text:
Windows blocks all PowerShell scripts by default. Your machine has no execution policy set at any level, so the default applies, and the README told you to run the `.ps1` directly. Run it like this instead:

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\wsl-network\wsl-network.ps1"
```

The bypass only applies to that one PowerShell process and doesn't change any Windows settings. `home/home.nix:134` already runs the chrome-devtools script the same way.

**Fix:** I updated both commands in `README.md` (the diagnostic and `-Recover`) to use this form. The script didn't change, so you don't need to rebuild.

**Tested:** I ran both commands from a standard Windows PowerShell 5.1 session:
- **Old command:** fails with the same error you got.
- **New command:** ran in about 9 seconds, exited with code 0, and saved a full report to `C:\Users\tteggel\AppData\Local\wsl-network\reports\wsl-network-20261021-120303-550.txt`. Networking was healthy: HTTPS requests by hostname and by IP worked from both Windows and WSL.
- **Guest routes section:** reports exit code 1, but only because `tailscale status` says "Logged out." The section's actual output is complete.

I haven't committed the README change.

If you'd rather keep the shorter `& "...ps1"` command, run `Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned` once in Windows PowerShell. That permanently loosens a Windows security setting, so I left it for you to decide.

mdv-previewer renders mdv's ANSI text, so there is nowhere to put an
image. Instead, wrap mdv: each ```mermaid fence is drawn in Unicode box
characters by merman-cli and spliced back in as a code block before the
real mdv sees the file. Files without a mermaid fence go straight
through.

Drawings are capped to the width mdv leaves inside a code block at that
heading depth, so mdv never wraps them. Anything merman can't draw as a
diagram (unsupported types, syntax errors, gantt and the other families
it only dumps as text, too wide for the pane) stays as source.
--version also reports merman's version so the previewer's render cache
re-renders.

merman is pinned to v0.8.0 because its CLI is still renaming flags, and
keeps its own nixpkgs: it's a several-minute Rust build with no binary
cache, so it should only rebuild when the tag moves.
